test_title: PYST 6: SSC CPO - General Intelligence and Reasoning (Held On 11 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: reasoning
question:
In the following question, two statements are followed by four conclusions. You have to assume the given statements to be true, if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Read the conclusions carefully and conclusions logically follows from the statements.

**Statements:**

No trains are buses

All buses are vehicles.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some trains are vehicles

II. No train is vehicle

III. All vehicles are buses

IV. Some vehicles are buses
solution:
Given Statements:

No trains are buses.

All buses are vehicles.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/69e0200f7bf8aaec8afb38494f87c16d48d08a72975f441828b2dda5cd44ee39.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some trains are vehicles - False (No relation is given between trains and vehicles, so this cannot be concluded)

II. No train is vehicle - False (We cannot assume trains are completely separate from vehicles, since no such statement is given)

III. All vehicles are buses - False (Given all buses are vehicles, but not all vehicles are buses, so this is incorrect)

IV. Some vehicles are buses - **True **(Since all buses are vehicles, it directly implies that some vehicles are buses)

So, Only Conclusion IV follows..

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 4".**
